title: A bell from dice
eyebrow: CETI · the central limit theorem, with dice
lede: 100,000 rolls of five dice land on a felt table as a flat field; seen from the side, sorted by their sum, they make a bell, and the count of the tail agrees with the exact count of ways.
captions: Random means anything can happen. Right?
Roll five dice and add them. This roll makes 18.
Is a sum above 25 as likely as one in the middle?
Now roll them 100,000 times. One mark is one roll.
Every roll counted in, in the order it was thrown.
100,000 rolls. Nothing smoothed, nothing left out.
Sort the same rolls by the first die alone.
Six piles, each between 16,519 and 16,797. Flat.
One die really is anything-can-happen.
Now sort by the sum: 26 piles, from 5 to 30.
From above, every sum looks just as likely.
From the side: 17 and 18 tower; the ends vanish.
Push in on the right edge: sums from 26 to 30.
Five thin piles. Now count every roll in them.
A cut travels along the sums, counting as it goes.
Above 25: 1,655 rolls out of 100,000.
That is 1.7 %. Equal odds would put 19,231 there.
Equal odds over-count the tail about 12 times.
Count the ways instead: 126 of 7,776 outcomes.
That predicts 1,620. The dice gave 1,655.
All 26 sums agree within 0.09 points. Mean 17.5.
Monday: is your total many small, separate parts?
Fair, independent dice. Linked parts break it.

brand.takeaway: Add many small chances and the middle wins.

sources: Abraham de Moivre, The Doctrine of Chances (2nd ed., with the 1733 approximation of the binomial by the normal curve) (1738). London: Woodfall
Pierre-Simon Laplace, Theorie analytique des probabilites (sums of many independent errors tend to the normal law) (1812). Paris: Courcier

Charles M. Grinstead, J. Laurie Snell, Introduction to Probability, 2nd rev. ed.: ch. 7 (sums of independent random variables, convolution of dice), ch. 9 (central limit theorem) (1997). American Mathematical Society; free PDF (GNU FDL)
Tommy Ettinger, Mulberry32, a 32-bit state PRNG (public domain) (2017). gist by tommyettinger; the arsenal's copy in arsenal/patterns/*/pattern.js
honest: Fair dice rolled independently; parts that move together, or one part that dwarfs the rest, do not make this bell.

knobs_doc.name: countT0
knobs_doc.what: s: second the first roll lands on the table (the lane is empty before it)

knobs_doc.name: countT1
knobs_doc.what: s: second the last of the rolls lands (the count reads all of them by 24.0)

knobs_doc.name: countWin
knobs_doc.what: share of the rolls that are still settling at once during the count-in (larger = softer front)

knobs_doc.name: hotFlash
knobs_doc.what: how long a newly landed roll stays bright, as a factor of the settling window

knobs_doc.name: waffPitch
knobs_doc.what: world units: spacing of the 500 x 200 field of rolls on the table

knobs_doc.name: waffFill
knobs_doc.what: share of the field spacing a mark fills (smaller = more felt between marks)

knobs_doc.name: cubePitch
knobs_doc.what: world units: spacing of the stacked marks (one box per roll); scales every stack

knobs_doc.name: cubeFill
knobs_doc.what: share of the stack spacing a box fills (smaller = a visible seam between rolls)

knobs_doc.name: fdW
knobs_doc.what: boxes across one first-die stack (the six stacks)

knobs_doc.name: fdD
knobs_doc.what: boxes deep in one first-die stack

knobs_doc.name: fdGap
knobs_doc.what: world units: air between the six first-die stacks

knobs_doc.name: sumW
knobs_doc.what: boxes across one sum stack (26 stacks; with sumGap it sets the width of the bell)

knobs_doc.name: sumD
knobs_doc.what: boxes deep in one sum stack (fewer = taller bell)

knobs_doc.name: sumGap
knobs_doc.what: world units: air between the 26 sum stacks

knobs_doc.name: fd0
knobs_doc.what: s: the first roll leaves the field for its first-die stack (arrival order)

knobs_doc.name: fdSpread
knobs_doc.what: s: from the first roll leaving to the last roll leaving (fd0 + fdSpread + fdFly <= 33.6)

knobs_doc.name: fdFly
knobs_doc.what: s: flight time of one roll from the field to its stack

knobs_doc.name: fdLift
knobs_doc.what: world units: hop height of a roll in flight to the first-die stacks

knobs_doc.name: sum0
knobs_doc.what: s: the first roll leaves its first-die stack for its sum stack

knobs_doc.name: sumSpread
knobs_doc.what: s: from the first roll leaving to the last (sum0 + sumSpread + sumFly <= 47.4)

knobs_doc.name: sumFly
knobs_doc.what: s: flight time of one roll to its sum stack

knobs_doc.name: sumLift
knobs_doc.what: world units: hop height of a roll in flight to the sum stacks

knobs_doc.name: diceT0
knobs_doc.what: s: the first of the five dice lands

knobs_doc.name: diceStep
knobs_doc.what: s: between one die landing and the next

knobs_doc.name: diceSize
knobs_doc.what: sheet units: edge of a die in the hook

knobs_doc.name: flatAt

knobs_doc.name: hookOut

knobs_doc.name: landAt

knobs_doc.name: pinsFirstOut

knobs_doc.what: s: the equal-odds line (3,846 per sum) appears over the sum stacks

knobs_doc.name: pinsSumAt
knobs_doc.what: s: the peak and end counts pin on their stacks (after the side view lands)

knobs_doc.name: tailLitAt
knobs_doc.what: s: the five tail stacks start to turn accent (1.2 s ramp)

knobs_doc.name: pinsTailAt
knobs_doc.what: s: the five tail counts pin on their stacks

knobs_doc.name: volIn
knobs_doc.what: s: the cross-fade from the stacks to the counted cells starts

knobs_doc.name: volCutDim

knobs_doc.what: s: the cut starts at sum 5

knobs_doc.name: cutT1
knobs_doc.what: s: the cut reaches the 25 / 26 edge (the tail count lands at tailAt)

knobs_doc.name: tailAt
knobs_doc.what: s: the tail cells light and the tail count lands (count 2)

knobs_doc.name: ratioAt
knobs_doc.what: s: the share appears under the tail count (always after it)

knobs_doc.name: beliefAt
knobs_doc.what: s: the equal-odds line and its tail box return

knobs_doc.name: timesAt
knobs_doc.what: s: "about 12 times too many" appears

knobs_doc.name: exactT0

knobs_doc.name: exactT1

knobs_doc.name: waysAt

knobs_doc.name: agreeAt

knobs_doc.name: cutOffAt

knobs_doc.name: bandAt
knobs_doc.what: s: the middle band (sums 14 to 21) lights

knobs_doc.what: how far rolls outside the band fade toward muted (1 = all the way)
